key_insight: AI rewriting can make radiology text look cleaner while actually weakening its alignment with the image—especially for standardized rewriting and teaching-case preparation.
clinical_relevance: For multimodal medical AI datasets, preserving clinical uncertainty and image-text fidelity may matter more than making reports stylistically uniform.
method: 450 chest X-ray reports from the Indiana University dataset
Generated three synthetic rewrites: EHR summarization, standardized rewriting, and teaching case preparation
Compared entity erosion, hedging loss, and BiomedCLIP image-text alignment changes
evidence_signal: EHR summarization erased 51.4% of clinical entities and 43.7% of hedging language but reduced alignment only 2.5%, while standardized rewriting and teaching-case preparation caused 14.9–16.5% alignment drops.
watch_item: Rare pathologies were not preferentially degraded in this study, so simple condition-specific monitoring may miss rewriting-induced contamination.
paper_title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports
